description:
Draft a new onboarding plan: one document describing everything a client's onboarding would change (task types, review policy, invitations, reviewers, lookup lists), each item with why it is there. Free.

A draft changes nothing in the organisation. It may be incomplete: handinloop_validate_onboarding_plan names what is missing. Every item needs a 'why', and may 'cite' the client's document it came from ({ document, page?, quote? }). Refused before anything is stored: a key the schema does not have (naming its path), and anything that looks like a secret: a plan never carries a credential, a person enters it in the product.

Never use handinloop_save_task_type for an onboarding: that changes the workspace at once, and a plan is what a person approves.

Needs an API key with the 'onboard' scope (#844), which is never on by default: an organisation admin or engineer ticks it on a new key (a key that had 'workflows' before #844 was given it). Without it the call fails naming the scope: ask a person for such a key rather than retrying.

Args:
  - document: { summary?, account_id?, task_types?, review_policy?, invitations?, reviewers?, lookup_sources? }. A task type is what handinloop_save_task_type takes, plus why and cite.

Returns: { plan_id, status: "draft", revision: 1, link, next_step }

account_id.description: The workspace the task types are saved on; with an API key, the key's own

invitations.description: People to invite: { email, role, why }

lookup_sources.description: The organisation's lookup lists (a HandInLoop operator applies these)

summary.description: The plan in a sentence or two, for the person approving it (up to 2000 characters)

task_types.description: Task types to add or replace whole: { id, name, fields, why, description?, line_item_schema?, export?, prompt_template?, gate?, review_policy?, cite? }

name: handinloop_draft_onboarding_plan
title: Draft an Onboarding Plan
